title: Removing a key from PostgreSQL's JSONB causes TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'dict' and 'str'

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Describe the bug

Removing a key from JSONB object raises an exception in synchronizing code. It works fine with SQLAlchemy 1.3.24.

### To Reproduce

```python
#!/usr/bin/python
from sqlalchemy import BigInteger, Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

engine = create_engine("postgresql://URI", echo=True)
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = Session()

Base = declarative_base()


class Demo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "demo"

    id = Column(BigInteger, primary_key=True)
    params = Column(JSONB, nullable=False, server_default="{}")


Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

target = Demo(params={"foo1": "bar", "foo2": "baz"})
session.add(target)
session.flush()
session.expunge(target)

# works fine if the next line is commented
prev_object = session.query(Demo).get(target.id)
session.query(Demo).filter(Demo.id == target.id).update(
    {Demo.params: Demo.params - "foo1"},
    # {Demo.params: {"foo2": "baz"}},  # this also works fine
    synchronize_session="fetch",
)
session.commit()
```
